current.text: LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are gone. Ball went to Minnesota in the deal that brought in Naz Reid. Bridges went to Phoenix for Royce O'Neale and Grayson Allen.
Ball was a 30-plus usage player. Losing Bridges frees about 32 minutes in the power forward and center mix.
Charlotte moved Ball and Bridges because it believes Kon Knueppel can do more. It chose to trade Bridges rather than pay him.
The open usage should go mainly to Coby White and Kon Knueppel.
No single lead creator is expected. Playmaking should be spread across White, Knueppel and Brandon Miller.
The biggest question is how White, Knueppel and Miller split the ball handling, and how that changes their efficiency.
Projected starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Naz Reid at power forward and Moussa Diabaté at center.
White starts over Dennis Schröder.
Grayson Allen starts while Knueppel is out. He would also start if Miller misses games early in the season.
The projected bench is Allen, Schröder, Hannes Steinbach, O'Neale and Grant Williams.
There is no trusted backup point guard on the roster.
The center plan is unclear. The choice is between Diabaté, the rookie taken 14th and Ryan Kalkbrenner.
Last season the team was better with Diabaté starting.
Charlotte will probably run a three-center rotation and also use Grant Williams as a small-ball five. Steinbach likely won't get near 30 minutes.
With Kai Jones, Diabaté and Kalkbrenner also in the frontcourt, Reid's minutes at center are limited.
Coach Charles Lee is expected to experiment with frontcourt lineups. The starters should stay stable, but closing lineups will vary by matchup.
The team is leaning fully into spacing the floor and will take a lot of threes.
The team also emphasizes steals and offensive rebounds.
Charlotte lost the passer who pushed its transition play. Its defense may be horrific.
The roster is deep, deeper than last season.
Charlotte looks like a play-in team, not an outright playoff team. Its 37.5 win total ranks 20th.
The team still has to waive three players. The Hield-for-Dillingham trade was made to lower the cost of waiving them.
Charlotte has a 40 million USD trade exception and could add a player at the trade deadline.
Charlotte has only 13 back-to-backs, the fewest in the league, so its players carry less rest risk.
The playoff schedule is 4-3-4 for 11 games, 4th best of 30. The only back-to-back pair is in week 19.
Charlotte plays only two games in the week starting March 1, the last week before our playoffs.

durable.text: The Hornets were cautious with LaMelo Ball, and some of his missed games were tied to tanking.
Last season the team did not let Kalkbrenner shoot threes. Steinbach was not allowed to shoot them in Summer League either. Its traditional centers are not used as three-point shooters.

note: With Ball and Bridges gone, Charlotte lifts Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller and Naz Reid. It plays a three-heavy style, has the fewest back-to-backs in the league and has an 11-game playoff schedule. The center minutes are split, which hurts Diabaté, Kalkbrenner and the rookies, and Grayson Allen is the first wing up as a starter. Early on, watch how White, Knueppel and Miller split the ball and how efficient they are, how long Knueppel is out, and who wins the center job.
